en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Nineteenth Chapter
Is emptiness included within the aggregate of mental formations? Yes.
Is the signless included within the aggregate of mental formations?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is emptiness included within the aggregate of mental formations?
“Yes.
“Then is the wishless included within the aggregate of mental formations?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is it not to be said of the signless that it is included in the aggregate of mental formations?
Yes, it is.
Should emptiness not be said to be "included within the aggregate of formations"? It should not be so said ... [and so on] ...
Is the wishless not to be described as "included in the aggregate of formations"? Yes.
Should emptiness not be said to be included within the aggregate of mental formations?
It should not be so said … [as before] … .
Is emptiness included within the aggregate of mental formations? Yes.

Then is the aggregate of mental formations not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently originated, and not subject to destruction, not subject to vanishing, not subject to fading away, not subject to cessation, and not subject to change?

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change? Yes, it is.
If the aggregate of formations is impermanent … [and so on] … subject to change, then indeed,
it should not be said that “emptiness is included within the aggregate of formations.”
Is the emptiness of the aggregate of form included within the aggregate of mental formations? Yes.
Is the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations included within the aggregate of form?
It should not be said thus …pe… [of] the aggregate of feeling …pe… [of] the aggregate of perception …pe….
Is the emptiness of the consciousness aggregate included within the formations aggregate?
Yes. Is the emptiness of the formations aggregate included within the consciousness aggregate?
It should not be said so… [as before] … Should it not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations is included within the aggregate of form?
“Yes.
Is the emptiness of the aggregate of form not to be described as “included within the aggregate of mental formations”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … it should not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations is included within the aggregate of feeling … [as before] …
“Are they included within the aggregate of perception … the aggregate of consciousness?
“Yes.”
Is the emptiness of the consciousness aggregate not to be described as "included within the aggregate of mental formations"?
It should certainly not be so described... [and so on].
Is it not to be said that emptiness is included within the aggregate of mental formations?
Yes, it is.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“This, bhikkhus, is empty of formations, whether of a self or of what belongs to a self”?
Is there such a sutta?
“Yes, [it is].
Therefore, emptiness is included within the aggregate of formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*).
The Discussion on Emptiness is finished.
